features.title: Add position_limits field to Account and Reason.POSITION_LIMIT (no behavior change)
acceptance: Account has `position_limits: dict[str, Decimal]` with default_factory=dict, declared AFTER `positions` so the existing positional call Account(id, margin, positions) still works and `position_limits=` is accepted as keyword
validate_order is unchanged; all of tests/ and invariants/test_order_invariants.py still pass
Unit test confirms Account defaults to empty position_limits and that two Accounts do not share the same dict
No float used anywhere; invariants/, factory.toml, CODEOWNERS and .github/ untouched

features.title: Enforce per-symbol position limit in validate_order for exposure-increasing orders only
acceptance: Add a small typed helper (e.g. `_breaches_position_limit(order, account) -> bool`) in orders/validation.py; the logic is: limit = account.position_limits.get(symbol); if limit is None return False; current = account.positions.get(symbol, Decimal(0)); new = current + signed_qty(order); breach only if abs(new) > abs(current) AND abs(new) > limit
Check runs after the structural checks (instrument/qty/lot/tick) and returns exactly one Reason.POSITION_LIMIT rejection; it is placed with the risk checks
Missing symbol in position_limits means no limit; a missing position is treated as Decimal(0)
Exactly at the limit is accepted (abs(new) == limit), one lot step over is rejected
Reducing or closing orders are never rejected with POSITION_LIMIT, including when the account is already over the limit (e.g. pos=+300, limit=100, SELL 1 is accepted)
A flip order (e.g. long 5 -> SELL 12 gives -7, limit 10) is accepted when abs(new) <= limit, and rejected when abs(new) > limit and abs(new) > abs(current)

New tests in tests/test_validation.py cover BUY and SELL, long and short and flat positions, at-limit, over-limit, reducing while over-limit, flip across zero, no limit configured, and limit for a different symbol only
validate_order does not mutate account or order (compare before/after in a test)
`python -m pytest -q tests/` and `python -m pytest -q invariants/` both pass (including invariants/test_position_limit_invariants.py); change is under ~100 lines

risks: Using abs(new) > limit alone (without the abs(new) > abs(current) guard) blocks reducing orders when already over the limit, which violates invariant 2 and AGENTS.md rule 5.
Checking the limit against order.qty instead of the resulting net position (current + signed_qty) gives wrong results for shorts and for BUY vs SELL; sign errors on SELL are easy to make.
Flip orders (long to short through zero) are neither plain reductions nor plain increases. Judge them by the final abs(new) vs abs(current), not by side alone.

Existing margin check runs on all orders, including reducing ones, so a reducing order can still be rejected for INSUFFICIENT_MARGIN. This is a pre-existing behavior that conflicts with AGENTS.md rule 5. The invariants use RICH margin so they will not catch it. Do not silently change it. Flag it in the notes for a human.

Check ordering: if the limit check runs before the margin check, an order failing both reports POSITION_LIMIT instead of INSUFFICIENT_MARGIN. Keep it with the risk checks and keep exactly one Reason per rejection.
A missing key must mean no limit. Do not use `.get(symbol, 0)` for the limit, because that would reject everything. Treat missing positions as 0 but missing limits as None.
Never convert to float or build Decimals from floats. Use Decimal(0), not 0.0. Mixing int literals is fine, float is not.
Adding the Account field in the wrong position, or without default_factory, breaks existing Account(...) callers and the shared mutable default.
Do not mutate account.positions or position_limits, for example by using setdefault. validate_order must stay pure.
Invariant files, factory.toml, CODEOWNERS and .github/ are human-owned. If an invariant looks wrong, stop and note it rather than editing.
